title: Shadows
examples: Teacher, why do shadows change size?
Can shadows happen when it is cloudy?

explain.say: Light travels in straight lines to reach us.
When light hits something, it can be blocked by an object.
The blocked light creates a dark shape called a shadow.
When the sun is high in the sky, shadows are quite short.
When the sun is low, like in the morning or evening, shadows are very long.
In real life, you see this when you play outside at different times.

faq.a: Shadows change size because the sun moves across the sky. When the sun is low, the light hits you at a slant, making the shadow long.
asks: Does the sun's position change shadow size?

faq.q: Can I make a shadow without the sun?
faq.a: Yes, you can use a flashlight or a lamp to make shadows indoors. You still need a light source to block the light.
asks: Do I need sunlight for shadows?
Can I use a torch for shadows?

faq.a: Shadows are shortest when the light source, like the sun, is directly overhead in the sky. This usually happens near noon.
asks: At what time are shadows shortest?

faq.a: A shadow is simply the area where an object blocks the path of light. It is not a real thing, but an absence of light.
asks: What is a shadow made of?

faq.q: Does the time of day change the shadow?
faq.a: Yes, the time of day changes the shadow greatly. In the morning, shadows are long, and at noon, they are short.
asks: What happens to shadows over the day?

facts: A shadow is formed when an object blocks light.
Shadows are longest in the early morning and late afternoon.
Shadows are shortest when the light source is highest.

quiz.say: If the sun is just rising, what will your shadow look like?
quiz.why: When the sun is low on the horizon, the light hits you at a shallow angle, making your shadow very long.

wrong.1: This is wrong because short shadows happen when the sun is high up in the sky.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you still need the object to block the light for a shadow to appear.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the sun's height changes the angle of the light all day long.

quiz.say: At what time of day are shadows usually the shortest?
quiz.why: When the sun is almost directly overhead at noon, the light rays hit the ground straight down, making the shadow tiny.

wrong.0: This is wrong because clouds block the sun, so you might not see any clear shadow at all.
wrong.2: This is wrong because early morning light is low, creating long shadows.
wrong.3: This is wrong because late afternoon light is also low, making shadows stretch out.

quiz.say: If you stand in the path of a flashlight beam, what do you create?
quiz.why: The flashlight acts like the sun, and your body blocks its straight beam of light, making a shadow.

wrong.0: This is wrong because rainbows need water droplets and sunlight, not just an object blocking light.
wrong.2: This is wrong because blocking light always results in less light, not more.
wrong.3: This is wrong because a reflection is light bouncing off a surface, not the absence of light.
